title: kv-residency-throttler-and-page-glue-allocator
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Introduces KV residency throttler and page-glue allocator to reduce fragmentation and spill congestion. Improves p95 request latency under memory pressure and reduces fallback spill events.
description:
Summary: Implements a two-part memory-management improvement for the KV cache: 1) a residency throttler that bounds concurrent large-evictor windows to avoid spill congestion and IO stalls, and 2) a page-glue allocator that opportunistically coalesces adjacent free pages to reduce fragmentation and improve long-run memory utilization. Motivation: production incidents in Dec showed multiple tenants triggering large simultaneous spillovers which caused a cascade of reclaim activity and elevated tail latency. Existing slab-like allocation kept fragmentation high under mixed-length keys and led to repeated small-page spills. This PR targets both the allocator hot path and scheduling policy to reduce those failure modes. Changes in this PR (high level): - Residency throttler: new lightweight controller that tracks in-flight eviction/spill tasks per pool, enforces soft limits, and provides backpressure signals to the scheduler. Configurable by tenant and pool; defaults tuned from observed traces. - Page-glue allocator: post-free fast path merges adjacent free pages within the same run; introduces a compactible-bit on page headers to mark regions eligible for glue passes during low-load windows. - Compact window scheduler: background compaction pass that prefers runs with high fragmentation score and low active references, integrates with residency throttler to avoid competing IO. - Allocation improvements: micro-optimizations in hot-path allocation (reduced CAS contention, improved free-list locality) and a fallback coarse-grained allocator for very large requests. - Metrics and tracing: new metrics (kv.residency.inflight, kv.residency.throttle_count, kv.page_glue.coalesces, kv.fragmentation.score) and traces added to critical paths for post-deploy analysis. - Tests: unit tests for allocator invariants, integration tests simulating mixed-length workloads and induced IO stalls, and a perf benchmark harness used for the PR numbers below. Commits (summary): - c1a2d3d: initial residency-throttler skeleton and config knobs - f4b5e6a: page-glue allocator implementation + page header bit - a7b8c9e: compact-window scheduler and prioritization heuristics - d0e1f2a: allocator hot-path CAS reduction + microbench - e3f4g5h: metrics, tracing, and unit tests - i6j7k8l: integration test for spill-congestion scenario + perf harness results - m9n0o1p: docs and default config tuning Files touched (high-level): - runtime/kv/allocator.cc (main allocator changes) - runtime/kv/allocator.h (interface additions) - runtime/kv/residency_throttler.cc/.h (new controller) - runtime/kv/compact_scheduler.cc/.h (background compaction) - runtime/kv/metrics.cc (new metrics) - tests/kv/allocator_test.cc (unit tests) - tests/kv/integration/spill_congestion_test.cc (integration) - infra/benchmarks/kv_fragment_bench.py (perf harness) - docs/ops/kv_tuning.md (operator-facing notes) Performance observations (bench): - Test setup: 8-GPU dedicated pool, 1M keys mixed sizes (8B-12KB), synthetic read/write distribution (70/30), bump workload to steady-state then induce ten concurrent tenants with bursty writes. - Baseline: before changes, steady-state p95 latency for serve path under pressure 210ms, and observed 18 large-spill events per minute leading to IO backpressure. - After changes (default knobs): p95 dropped to 160ms (24% improvement), large-spill events reduced to 5/min, average memory fragmentation score improved by ~32%. - With aggressive glue/compaction settings: p95 140ms, spill events 2/min but CPU overhead for compaction increased ~6%. CI and rollout plan: - CI: unit + integration + perf-smoke now run in parallel. Initial CI run failed a flaky integration test on macOS runners (timeout), fixed by increasing test timeouts and adding a deterministic seed for allocator randomness. Final CI status: pass. - Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag for 2 weeks in canary tenants, collect metrics kv.residency.* and kv.page_glue.* and then progressively enable for all dedicated pools. Review conversation (high level, single-string): "Marta: Can you explain how the throttler signal is delivered to the scheduler? Are we relying on a shared atomic or a queue? Please add comments around the memory model.
Priya: Throttler exposes a non-blocking counter + leaky-bucket token refill; scheduler observes via an atomic snapshot and uses a best-effort yield. Added detailed comments in residency_throttler.h and a short design note.
Jin: We need more tests for pathological alternating allocate/free patterns that could defeat glueing.
Priya: Added allocator_test.cc::GlueRaceSimulation which runs 10k randomized ops with deterministic seed; added asserts to verify no double-free and no lost pages.
Liam: Curious about metric cardinality — do we tag by tenant?
Priya: yes, metrics are tagged by pool_id and tenant_id; added sampling for high-cardinality tenants in metrics.cc (default off).
Marta: Approve after CI green.
Jin: Approve.
Liam: Approved and requested squash-merge." Merge outcome: "Merged by Marta Alvarez using squash and merge. Merge commit message: 'kv: residency throttler + page-glue allocator — reduce fragmentation and spill congestion (ENG-5421)'." Notes on observability and ops: "docs/ops/kv_tuning.md" includes recommended default knobs and a troubleshooting checklist (how to interpret kv.residency.throttle_count spikes, when to raise glue frequency, how to temporarily disable glue on CPU-constrained nodes). Backwards compatibility: allocator ABI unchanged; config knobs are additive. Risk and mitigations: - Risk: compaction could add CPU pressure. Mitigation: compaction runs capped by residency throttler and defaulted to run only during low utilization windows; operators can tune glue frequency. - Risk: new code path could expose rare race. Mitigation: added deterministic fuzz test in CI and a limited canary rollout. Related work: this complements previous KV improvements (segment coalescer PRs) by focusing on run-time residency and small-page fragmentation. Linked Linear tasks: ENG-5421 (residency throttler design), ENG-5499 (allocator glue prototype).
